title: Planar STL boundary extraction and Gmsh 2D generation
overview: Reads one planar STL body loop, reconstructs its boundary, and generates Gmsh 2D geometry for directly bounded planar regions, external-flow obstacle domains, and internal-flow channels. Directly bounded planar regions also support automatic unstructured TRI_3 meshing controlled by mesh_size without transfinite cell counts.
principle: STL facets carry coordinates and triangle topology, not standard CFD boundary-condition semantics. Singly incident triangle edges reconstruct the body loop. A sidecar either assigns names to a planar region boundary or defines a rectangular external-flow domain whose four sides are Inlet, Outlet, Symmetry and Farfield and whose internal STL loop is Wall. Physical names require a separate mapping to OneFLOW BC semantics. External flow constructs a fluid surface by subtracting an internal obstacle loop from an enclosing outer loop; internal flow uses the STL boundary loop itself as the closed fluid-domain boundary. Both assign physical names independently of solver boundary-state configuration.
architecture: Native C++: STL -> StlMeshReader -> tolerance-based vertex welding and single planar boundary loop -> explicit Case layout JSON -> Gmsh .geo -> configured Gmsh CLI -> MSH 4.1 -> existing C++ Gmsh reader and topology/Physical Group validation. Each STL-to-Gmsh geometry family groups mesh-topology variants (for example square/single_quad and square/two_triangles), with Native C++ and Python Reference implementations beneath each variant; Python geometry uses grid/stl/stl_to_gmsh.py. The former root-level preprocessing script was retired to prevent source-tree output pollution. The cube_single_hex native and Python implementations independently validate an axis-aligned cube STL, reconstruct six surfaces and one volume in the existing GridConversion module, and require one HEXA_8 cell plus six QUAD_4 boundary faces. The square_2x2 native Case reuses the exact square STL and changes only its transfinite layout. The shared Mesh-to-CFD Validation Workbench builds an artifact-bound STL -> Gmsh -> CGNS -> OneFLOW -> CFD Case graph, validates MSH 4.1 topology and Physical Groups, and retains per-stage logs and validation reports in a user-data workspace outside the source tree. Omission of transfinite_cells selects automatic triangular meshing in both C++ and Python; mesh_size controls target element size, not an exact cell count. Automatic output is checked with boundary-edge incidence and the Euler characteristic instead of fixed element totals.

proves: ASCII and binary STL triangle records can be read and a planar square fixture yields one four-edge boundary loop.
The planar STL loop can be used as an internal wall hole inside an explicitly bounded rectangular fluid domain.
The four outer rectangle sides and internal wall are emitted as separate named Gmsh Physical Curve groups.
The native C++ Grid conversion route accepts STL as source and Gmsh as target for a single axis-aligned rectangular XY boundary with explicit transfinite cell counts.
The native C++ route validates generated MSH 4.1 node counts, LINE_2 and QUAD_4 element counts, and the four outer Physical Curve names plus fluid_domain.
The square and two_square_cells native C++ Cases and their independent Python references are registered separately in the grid Case catalog.
The square_2x2 native Case reuses the square STL geometry and changes only the transfinite layout to produce a 2 x 2 quadrilateral mesh.
The shared Mesh-to-CFD Validation Workbench declares artifact handoffs through Gmsh MSH 4.1, CGNS, a native OneFLOW grid, and a staged CFD consumer, using isolated Case workspaces.
The Python external-flow reference Case builds a rectangular fluid domain with a polygonal STL obstacle as a named internal Wall boundary.
The Python internal-flow reference Case uses a closed rectangular STL loop as the fluid-domain boundary and emits named inlet, outlet and wall Physical Curves.
The channel reference Case generates a deterministic 20 x 5 transfinite quadrilateral mesh, while the unstructured external-flow Case validates minimum mesh counts and exact Physical Group names.
The native C++ STL-to-Gmsh Case builds a 2D external-flow fluid domain by enclosing a planar STL body loop in a rectangular outer domain and creating a Plane Surface with the body as a hole.
The native C++ and Python circle external-flow Cases use byte-identical STL input and matching domain bounds, mesh-size controls and Physical Group names.

The native circle external-flow Case is registered for both Run Development Cases and Mesh-to-CFD Validation; the latter executes the selected MSH through the existing CGNS, OneFLOW-grid and CFD smoke-test chain.
The native C++ and independent Python cube_single_hex Cases validate a closed axis-aligned cube STL with twelve triangles and generate exactly one HEXA_8 volume cell with six QUAD_4 boundary faces.

The cube_single_hex Case pair is registered in Run Development Cases, Python Reference Cases and Mesh-to-CFD Validation; its validation graph checks MSH-to-CGNS-to-OneFLOW topology, boundary-region-map handoff and a two-step CFD smoke run using the staged laminar flat-plate template with dimension overridden to 3.

The legacy root-level script/run.py and its root input/results/script data were removed; Python reference Cases reject execution from checked-in source directories, and Python unit tests live under tests/python/grid.

The same unit-square STL and four named outer boundaries can produce either one QUAD_4 cell or exactly two TRI_3 cells by enabling or disabling Gmsh surface recombination while retaining a 1 x 1 transfinite boundary layout.

The native C++ planar STL-to-Gmsh route supports an automatic unstructured TRI_3 mode when transfinite_cells is omitted, validates boundary-edge incidence and the Euler characteristic, and reports the configured mesh size without asserting an exact cell count.
The Python reference geometry generator emits the same automatic mesh-size controls without transfinite constraints or recombination when transfinite_cells is omitted.
does_not_prove: Generated outer-flow meshes have been converted through CGNS into a OneFLOW native grid.
Generated MSH has been converted through CGNS into a OneFLOW native grid.
Boundary names are automatically translated into OneFLOW solver boundary-condition types.
Arbitrary plane orientations, holes, multiple components, curved reconstruction or general multi-cell meshing are supported.
The native STL-to-Gmsh C++ conversion has compiled and executed successfully on Windows and Linux; matching C++ tests are linked but still require CI execution evidence.
Generated MSH 4.1 has been automatically chained through Gmsh-to-CGNS and into a OneFLOW native grid by the same Case.
Gmsh Physical Curve names have been converted into solver boundary-condition state values.
The complete STL-to-CFD workflow has been executed successfully on Windows and Linux.
A successful CFD smoke run establishes numerical accuracy, convergence, conservation, boundary-condition correctness, or grid independence.
The new external- and internal-flow reference Cases have been converted through CGNS into OneFLOW native grids.
The external- and internal-flow reference Cases have been run through OneFLOW CFD or establish physical accuracy.
The circle external-flow CFD smoke test establishes an accurate cylinder wake, drag coefficient, lift coefficient or Strouhal number.

General STL-to-volume meshing, arbitrary closed surfaces, non-axis-aligned cubes, hybrid/prismatic strategies, or general hexahedral meshing are not supported by the restricted cube_single_hex prototype.
The exact triangle count or a strict monotonic element-count relationship for every Gmsh version and mesh-size ratio; mesh_size is a target size, not an exact element-count request.
